mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high FEDFUNDS growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) predict negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as weak labor market and weak demand jointly depress growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening coupled with demand softening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the combined signal in at least 70% of similar events (backtest failure).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% suggests accelerating economic momentum, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant relationship detected between INDPRO acceleration and SPX 20-day returns in out-of-sample tests (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months is expected to produce positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as expectations of lower future inflation boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in 60-day windows following CPIAUCSL < 2% for three months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% triggers a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6% in a given month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during UNRATE > 6% episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of below-target FEDFUNDS rates (below 1.5%) combined with elevated industrial production (INDPRO > 105) predict positive 20-day SPX returns as policy easing supports demand.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for two consecutive months AND INDPRO > 105 in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive when both triggers are met but FEDFUNDS remains above 1.5% in some months (out-of-sample failure).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) followed by a rebound above 2% within the same month signals a shifting inflation expectation, which is associated with negative 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% then crosses above 2% in the same month
failure_condition: No consistent negative returns when the CPIAUCSL shift pattern is not detected in the data (failure to detect pattern in 30% of test windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as dual softness signals recession risk.
regime_hint: dual soft labor and consumption demand
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite combined weakness in PAYEMS and HOUST (in >50% of similar events).
